Evolution module

NLO QCD evolution of moment space GPD. Many credits to K. Kumericki at https://github.com/kkumer/gepard.

Note

Functions in this module have as first argument Mellin moment n = j + 1, where j is conformal moment used everywhere else. Thus, they should always be called as f(j+1, …).

gumpgpd.Evolution.AlphaS(nloop: int, nf: int, Q: float) → float[source]

Running strong coupling \(\alpha_s(Q)\) at LO or NLO.

Dispatches to AlphaS0() (one-loop) or AlphaS1() (two-loop Runge-Kutta).

Parameters:

  • nloop (int) – Loop order; 1 for LO, 2 for NLO.

  • nf (int) – Number of active quark flavors.

  • Q (float) – Renormalization scale in GeV.

Returns:

\(\alpha_s(Q)\).

Return type:

float

Raises:

ValueError – If nloop is not 1 or 2.

gumpgpd.Evolution.AlphaS0(nf: int, Q: float) → float[source]

One-loop running strong coupling \(\alpha_s(Q)\).

Parameters:

  • nf (int) – Number of active quark flavors.

  • Q (float) – Renormalization scale in GeV.

Returns:

\(\alpha_s(Q)\) at leading order.

Return type:

float

gumpgpd.Evolution.AlphaS1(nf: int, Q: float) → float[source]

Two-loop running strong coupling \(\alpha_s(Q)\) via 4th-order Runge-Kutta.

Evolves the coupling from Ref_Scale to Q by integrating the two-loop beta function with NASTPS = 20 equal logarithmic steps.

Parameters:

  • nf (int) – Number of active quark flavors.

  • Q (float) – Renormalization scale in GeV.

Returns:

\(\alpha_s(Q)\) at next-to-leading order.

Return type:

float

gumpgpd.Evolution.CFF_Evo_LO(j: array, nf: int, p: int, mu: float, ConfFlav: array) → array[source]

Leading order evolution of the combination of DVCS Wilson coefficient and conformal moments

Parameters:

  • j – conformal spin j (conformal spin is actually j+2 but anyway): array (N,)

  • nf – number of effective fermions; scalar

  • p (int) – 1 for vector-like GPD (Ht, Et), -1 for axial-vector-like GPDs (Ht, Et); scalars

  • mu – final evolution scale; scalar

  • ConfFlav – uneolved conformal moments in flavor space ConfFlav = [ConfMoment_uV, ConfMoment_ubar, ConfMoment_dV, ConfMoment_dbar, ConfMoment_g]; shape (N,5)

Returns:

Evolved conformal moments times the DVCS Wilson coefficients in the evolution basis (qVal, q_du_plus, q_du_minus, qSigma, g); ingredients for the Mellin-Barnes integral for CFF return shape (N, 5)

Note

j accepts 1-D array input for the Mellin-Barnes contour integral; all other arguments should be scalar (or broadcastable with j).

gumpgpd.Evolution.CFF_Evo_NLO_evMOM(j: array, nf: int, p: int, Q: float, t: float, xi: float, Para: array, momshift: int, muf: float) → array[source]

Next-to-leading order evolved conformal moments combined with the DVCS Wilson coefficients in the evolution space (Evolved moment method)

Parameters:

  • j – conformal spin j (conformal spin is actually j+2 but anyway): array (N,)

  • nf – number of effective fermions;

  • p (int) – 1 for vector-like GPD (Ht, Et), -1 for axial-vector-like GPDs (Ht, Et): scalar

  • Q – final evolution scale: scalar

  • t – momentum transfer squared

  • xi – skewness

  • ConfFlav – unevolved conformal moments

  • Para – parameters of the conformal moments

  • momshift – shift of moments

  • muset – offset in the scale mu to study the scale dependence of the CFF

  • above (More notes in Moment_Evo_NLO() function)

Returns:

Next-to-leading order evolved conformal moments combined with the DVCS Wilson coefficients in the evolution basis (qVal, q_du_plus, q_du_minus, qSigma, g); return shape (N, 5)

Note

j accepts 1-D array input for the Mellin-Barnes contour integral; all other arguments should be scalar (or broadcastable with j).

gumpgpd.Evolution.CFF_Evo_NLO_evWC(j: array, nf: int, p: int, Q: float, ConfFlav: array, muf: float) → array[source]

Next-to-leading order evolved DVCS Wilson coefficients in the flavor space combined with the conformal moments (Evolved Wilson coefficient method)

Parameters:

  • j – conformal spin j (conformal spin is actually j+2 but anyway): array (N,)

  • nf – number of effective fermions; scalars

  • p (int) – 1 for vector-like GPD (Ht, Et), -1 for axial-vector-like GPDs (Ht, Et); scalars

  • Q (float) – photon virtuality. At NLO the scale Q enters the amplitudes through logs.

  • ConfFlav – uneolved conformal moments in flavor space ConfFlav = [ConfMoment_uV, ConfMoment_ubar, ConfMoment_dV, ConfMoment_dbar, ConfMoment_g]; shape (N,5)

  • meson (int) – 1 for rho, 2 for phi, 3 for Jpsi

  • muf – factorization evolution scale; scalar

Returns:

Evolved conformal moments times the DVCS Wilson coefficients in the evolution basis (qVal, q_du_plus, q_du_minus, qSigma, g); Ingredients for the Mellin-Barnes integral for TFF return shape (N, 5)

Note

j accepts 1-D array input for the Mellin-Barnes contour integral; all other arguments should be scalar (or broadcastable with j).

Leading order evolution of moments in the flavor space for non-singlet vector moments

Parameters:

  • j – conformal spin j (conformal spin is actually j+2 but anyway): shape (N,)

This function deals with the j=0 singularity in the Moment_Evo_LO(). We only evaluate the j=0 contributions for the charge odd terms

gumpgpd.Evolution.Moment_Evo_NLO(j: array, nf: int, p: int, mu: float, t: float, xi: float, Para: array, momshift: int) → array[source]

Next-to-leading order evolution of the conformal moments (Evolved moment method)

Parameters:

  • j – conformal spin j (conformal spin is actually j+2 but anyway): array (N,)

  • nf – number of effective fermions; scalars

  • p (int) – 1 for vector-like GPD (Ht, Et), -1 for axial-vector-like GPDs (Ht, Et); scalars

  • mu – factorization evolution scale; scalar

  • t – momentum transfer squared

  • xi – skewness

  • Para – parameters of the conformal moments

  • momshift (CAUTION!) – shift of moments

  • Note – xi,t are need when for the evolution of moments: We need Para for the parameters rather than just the unevolved moment ConFlav; Because the off-diagonal terms requires shift of moments.

  • momshift – When we shift the moment by j -> j+2 for xi^2 terms, only the evolution kernel E_{jk} should be shifted into E_{j+2,k+2}, whereas terms like xi^{-j-1} should not be shifted therefore, we should write the expression as E_{j,k+momshift} and x^{-j+momshift-1} to compensate/cancel the shift of j when j->j+2 is performed (momshift=2 in this case) Only relevant in the off-diagonal part

Returns:

Evolved conformal moment in evolution basis (qVal, q_du_plus, q_du_minus, qSigma, g); To be combined with the corresponding Wilson coefficient (for TFF/CFF) or conformal wave function (for GPD) return shape (N, 5)

Note

j accepts 1-D array input for the Mellin-Barnes contour integral; all other arguments should be scalar (or broadcastable with j).

gumpgpd.Evolution.S1(z: complex | ndarray) → complex | ndarray[source]

Harmonic sum S_1(z).

Parameters:

z – Complex argument.

Returns:

S_1(z) = sum_{k=1}^{z} 1/k (analytically continued via the digamma function).

gumpgpd.Evolution.S1_tilde(n: complex | ndarray, sgtr: int) → complex | ndarray[source]

Alternating harmonic sum S1-tilde with signature sgtr.

Defined in Eq. (39) of https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9810241.

Parameters:

  • n – Complex Mellin moment.

  • sgtr (int) – Signature factor sgtr = p * prty; +1 or -1.

Returns:

sgtr * (psi((n+2)/2) - psi((n+1)/2)) / 2 - log(2).

gumpgpd.Evolution.S2(z: complex | ndarray) → complex | ndarray[source]

Harmonic sum S_2(z).

Parameters:

z – Complex argument.

Returns:

S_2(z) = sum_{k=1}^{z} 1/k^2 (analytically continued via the trigamma function).

gumpgpd.Evolution.S2_prime(z: complex | ndarray, prty: int) → complex | ndarray[source]

Symmetrized harmonic sum S_2’ used in NLO splitting functions.

Defined in Eq. (5.29) of https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0550321380900036

Parameters:

  • z – Complex argument.

  • prty (int) – Signature factor; +1 or -1.

Returns:

(1 + prty)/2 * S2(z) + (1 - prty)/2 * S2(z - 1/2).

gumpgpd.Evolution.S2_tilde(n: complex | ndarray, sgtr: int) → complex | ndarray[source]

Alternating harmonic sum S2-tilde with signature sgtr.

Defined in Eq. (41) of https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9810241.

Parameters:

  • n – Complex Mellin moment.

  • sgtr (int) – Signature factor; +1 or -1.

Returns:

-zeta(2)/2 - sgtr * (psi^(1)((n+2)/2) - psi^(1)((n+1)/2)) / 4.

gumpgpd.Evolution.S2_tilde_KM(n, sgtr)[source]

Alternating harmonic sum S2-tilde as implemented in Gepard (K. Kumericki).

Parameters:

  • n – Complex Mellin moment.

  • sgtr (int) – Signature factor; +1 or -1.

Returns:

-5/8*zeta(3) + sgtr*(S1(n)/n^2 - zeta(2)/2*G + MellinF2(n)) where G = psi((n+1)/2) - psi(n/2).

gumpgpd.Evolution.S3(z: complex | ndarray) → complex | ndarray[source]

Harmonic sum S_3(z).

Parameters:

z – Complex argument.

Returns:

S_3(z) = sum_{k=1}^{z} 1/k^3 (analytically continued via the polygamma function).

gumpgpd.Evolution.S3_prime(z: complex | ndarray, prty: int) → complex | ndarray[source]

Symmetrized harmonic sum S_3’ used in NLO splitting functions.

Defined in Eq. (5.29) of https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0550321380900036

Parameters:

  • z – Complex argument.

  • prty (int) – Signature factor; +1 or -1.

Returns:

(1 + prty)/2 * S3(z) + (1 - prty)/2 * S3(z - 1/2).

gumpgpd.Evolution.S3_tilde(n: complex | ndarray, sgtr: int) → complex | ndarray[source]

Alternating harmonic sum S3-tilde with signature sgtr.

Defined in Eqs. (47) and (37) of https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9810241.

Parameters:

  • n – Complex Mellin moment.

  • sgtr (int) – Signature factor; +1 or -1.

Returns:

sgtr/2 * psi^(2)((n+2)/2 - psi^(2)((n+1)/2)) / 8 - 3/4 * zeta(3).

gumpgpd.Evolution.S4(z: complex | ndarray) → complex | ndarray[source]

Harmonic sum S_4(z).

Parameters:

z – Complex argument.

Returns:

S_4(z) = sum_{k=1}^{z} 1/k^4 (analytically continued via the polygamma function).

gumpgpd.Evolution.SB3(j: complex | ndarray) → complex | ndarray[source]

Special harmonic-sum combination SB3.

Defined in Eq. (4.44e) of https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.5394.

Parameters:

j – Complex argument.

Returns:

The combination 0.5*S1(j)*(-S2(-0.5+0.5*j)+S2(0.5*j)) + ....

gumpgpd.Evolution.Sm2p1(n: complex | ndarray, sgtr: int) → complex | ndarray[source]

Special combination Sm2p1 appearing in NLO DGLAP kernels.

Defined in Eq. (50) of https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9810241.

Parameters:

  • n – Complex Mellin moment.

  • sgtr (int) – Signature factor; +1 or -1.

Returns:

-sgtr * MellinF2(n+1) + zeta(2)*S1_tilde(n, sgtr) - 5/8*zeta(3) + zeta(2)*log(2).

gumpgpd.Evolution.Sp1m2(n: complex | ndarray, sgtr: int) → complex | ndarray[source]

Special combination Sp1m2 appearing in NLO DGLAP kernels.

Defined in Eq. (131) of https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9810241.

Parameters:

  • n – Complex Mellin moment.

  • sgtr (int) – Signature factor; +1 or -1.

Returns:

S1(n)*S2_tilde(n, sgtr) + S3_tilde(n, sgtr) - Sm2p1(n, sgtr).

gumpgpd.Evolution.TFF_Evo_NLO_evWC(j: array, nf: int, p: int, Q: float, ConfFlav: array, meson: int, muf: float) → array[source]

Next-to-leading order evolved DVMP Wilson coefficients in the flavor space combined with the conformal moments (Evolved Wilson coefficient method)

  • muf – factorization evolution scale; scalar

Returns:

j accepts 1-D array input for the Mellin-Barnes contour integral; all other arguments should be scalar (or broadcastable with j).

gumpgpd.Evolution.amuindep(j: complex, nf: int, p: int, prty: int = 1)[source]

Scale-independent part of the singlet diagonal NLO evolution operator.

Computes the P[gamma]P projector contraction appearing in the NLO singlet evolution matrix A (Eq. (124) of https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0703179). Unlike the Gepard implementation, there is no extra 1/beta_0 prefactor here; it cancels with the corresponding factor in rmudep().

Parameters:

  • j (complex) – Conformal spin j (note: n = j + 1 is passed internally).

  • nf (int) – Number of active quark flavors.

  • p (int) – 1 for vector-like GPDs (H, E), -1 for axial-vector-like GPDs (Ht, Et).

  • prty (int, optional) – C-parity; +1 for singlet, -1 for minus-sector. Defaults to 1.

Returns:

Shape (N, 2, 2, 2, 2) — the P[gamma]P part of the diagonal NLO evolution operator A at conformal spin j.

Return type:

np.ndarray

gumpgpd.Evolution.amuindepNS(j: complex, nf: int, p: int, prty: int = 1)[source]

Scale-independent part of the non-singlet diagonal NLO evolution operator.

Computes the anomalous-dimension factor in the NLO NS evolution matrix A (Eq. (124) of https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0703179).

Parameters:

  • j (complex) – Conformal spin j (note: n = j + 1 is passed internally).

  • nf (int) – Number of active quark flavors.

  • p (int) – 1 for vector-like GPDs (H, E), -1 for axial-vector-like GPDs (Ht, Et).

  • prty (int, optional) – C-parity; +1 for NS+, -1 for NS-. Defaults to 1.

Returns:

The scale-independent NS part of the diagonal NLO evolution operator A at conformal spin j.

Return type:

complex or np.ndarray

B^{jk}

gumpgpd.Evolution.fixed_quadvec(func, a, b, n=100, args=())[source]

Gaussian quadrature integration for vector-valued integrands.

Integrates func over [a, b] using an n-point Gauss-Legendre rule. Unlike scipy.integrate.fixed_quad(), the integrand may return an array of any trailing shape (not just a scalar), making it suitable for batched Mellin-Barnes contour integrals.

Parameters:

  • func – Callable with signature func(y) -> np.ndarray, where y has shape (n,) and the output has shape (n, ...).

  • a (float) – Lower integration limit.

  • b (float) – Upper integration limit.

  • n (int) – Number of quadrature points. Defaults to 100.

  • args (tuple) – Reserved for API compatibility; not forwarded to func.

Returns:

Approximation of \(\int_a^b \mathrm{func}(y)\,dy\), with shape matching the trailing dimensions of func’s output.

Return type:

np.ndarray

gumpgpd.Evolution.singlet_NLO(n: complex, nf: int, p: int, prty: int = 1) → ndarray[source]

Singlet NLO anomalous dimensions matrix.

Axial-case two-loop singlet anomalous dimensions from https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9506451 Eqs. (3.75)-(3.77). The identity S_{12}(n) + S_{21} = S_1(n)S_2(n) + S_3 (from https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9810241 Eq. (129)) was applied in the axial part of gg1.

Parameters:

  • n (complex) – Which moment (Mellin moment for integer n).

  • nf (int) – Number of active quark flavors.

  • p (int) – 1 for vector-like GPDs (H, E), -1 for axial-vector-like GPDs (Ht, Et).

  • prty (int) – C parity.

Returns:

Matrix (LO, NLO) where each is in turn 2x2 complex matrix ((QQ, QG), (GQ, GG))
